observability.permission.observability_a: Switch AI assistance on or off for this workspace, choose which providers may receive evidence, set the daily cap and the opt-in tracing of model calls.

Ask the investigator, draft status updates and post-mortems, ask questions of the telemetry in plain language, see the noise suggestions and the AI usage. Only works where the workspace has switched AI on; results are advisory and cite their evidence.
Acknowledge and resolve alerts, create silences, edit routing rules, integrations and dependencies. Announcing to the public status page stays observability.status.publish.

See alerts, routing rules, silences, ingest integrations and the dependency graph. ADMIN-floored on purpose: alert labels and annotations carry operational detail, and the monitors.read floor (MEMBER, S11) is a known defect this permission must not inherit.
observability.permission.observability_c: Connect, change, test and remove the Slack and Microsoft Teams channels that incident updates are posted to. The webhook URL is write-only: it is stored encrypted and is never shown again. Reading the list (hosts and settings only) needs observability.incidents.read.
observability.permission.observability_e: Close a contribution the extension breaker paused so it runs again at once, or keep it paused until a time; a reason is required and audited. A workspace acts on its own contributions; the system scope, other tenants and community plugin versions are the platform operator's (root tenant, behind the admin gate).
Which contributions the extension breaker has paused after repeated errors, why and until when. The root tenant can list every tenant's.
Any signed-in member's browser reports a contributed component that failed to render, so it is counted with the contribution's other failures.
observability.permission.observability_i: Put an incident on, or release it from, a legal hold. A held incident, its post-mortem and its linked alerts are never removed by a retention sweep. Narrow on purpose: it overrides the workspace's retention.
Resolve incidents and post progress updates. Publishing to the public page is NOT included — that is observability.status.publish.
Read an incident's timeline, roles, notes, follow-ups, changes and post-mortem, the update templates and the incident analytics.
observability.permission.observability_l: Create private probe locations, set their target allow-lists, enrol and revoke runners. The ROOT tenant also publishes the public locations.
See the probe locations this workspace can use, their runners and their target allow-lists.
observability.permission.observability_p: Root tenant only: the platform process registry screen.
observability.permission.observability_s: See the picture a browser check took at the step that failed. Its own permission and ADMIN-floored on purpose: the page under test can show anything (a signed-in account, a customer's data), and observability.monitors.read is the MEMBER-floored one.
Root tenant only: this process's request-latency percentiles and error ratio.
Create, change and delete SLOs and import OpenSLO documents.
See SLOs, their error budgets, burn rates and OpenSLO exports.
Create and change status pages, groups, translations, automations and subscribers. Publishing something outward (public page, embed, host, auto-publish) also takes observability.status.publish.
Flip an incident public/private. Separate and narrow on purpose: this is an outward-facing act that customers and subscribers see.
Publish to the public status page
Read the status pages, groups, translations, templates and subscribers of the tenant.
Lets the status page gate ask the platform guard whether the caller is a signed-in member of the tenant (AUTHENTICATED audience). Grants nothing by itself.
observability.permission.observability_t: Irreversibly erase this workspace's stored logs, traces and metrics (owner only; needs the workspace id typed back; audited).
Save and delete explorer queries and request a per-workspace retention from the telemetry backend.
Root tenant only: send raw LogQL, PromQL or TraceQL to the backend. Other workspaces never get this mode.
Query this workspace's own logs, traces and metrics with structured queries (never raw backend syntax), view the service map, correlate signals and list saved queries.

observability.telemetry.browser.public: A browser key is public: anyone who opens your page source can copy it. So create it with the scope telemetry:browser:write only (it writes browser_* metrics and logs, never traces), list the exact origins that may use it below, and keep the rate low. The origin list stops other websites from reusing the key; it cannot stop a script that sends the header by hand, which is why the scope, the rate limit and the size cap exist, and why you can revoke the key in one click.
